h1: The 6 Best Docking Stations with 100W Power Delivery of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: six docking stations with 100W or higher power delivery, compared on display support, ports, certification and price.
summary: The Plugable Thunderbolt 4 dock is our top pick, certified and driverless with 100W charging. The Anker Prime 14-port dock is the powerhouse for charging many devices, and the WAVLINK 13-in-1 offers 130W and dual 5K via DisplayLink. The UGREEN Revodok Pro and Acer 11-in-1 are the budget buys.
intro: A dock that says 100W does not always charge your laptop at 100W while it also runs monitors and drives. The headline figure is often the total budget the dock shares across everything plugged in, so a laptop that needs 90W can end up starved once peripherals draw their share.

We reviewed eight docks and ranked six, comparing power rating, display support, certification and ports. Wattage claims and port lists decide the ranking, backed by user reports, with nobench measurements, and prices are buckets. We left out a triple-HDMI dock with mixed refresh rates and a near-duplicate of the Anker line.

products.name: Plugable Thunderbolt 4 Dock (TBT-UDM), 100W Charging
products.verdict: Certified Thunderbolt 4, driverless, and built for new MacBooks.
products.description:
The Plugable TBT-UDM is Thunderbolt 4 certified, rated for 100W power delivery, and supports dual 4K HDMI or a single 6K display. It offers six USB ports, an SD slot and Ethernet, and needs no drivers on Mac or Windows. It sits in the $100-200 bucket.

It ranks first because certification means the bandwidth is verified, not just a USB4 label. Compared with the WAVLINK, it gives up the 130W rating and the dual 5K via DisplayLink.

It suits MacBook Air and Pro owners on M4 or M5 chips. The caveat is that 100W is the ceiling.
products.idealFor: Mac and Windows users who want verified Thunderbolt.

products.name: Anker Prime Docking Station, 14-Port, 160W Max Output
products.verdict: The largest power budget and port count here.
products.description:
The Anker Prime is a 14-port dock with 160W maximum output, 10Gbps data transfer, dual 4K display support, Ethernet and audio. It is compatible with Dell, HP, Lenovo and more and sits in the $100-200 bucket.

It takes the silver spot since the 160W total can charge a laptop plus hungry peripherals, which the Plugable cannot match, but it is not Thunderbolt certified in its listing.

It suits desks with many devices. The caveat is that dual 4K is the display ceiling.

products.name: WAVLINK USB C Docking Station, 13-in-1, 130W PD
products.verdict: 130W and dual high-resolution displays across Mac chips.
products.description:
The WAVLINK is a 13-in-1 dock rated for 130W PD with dual 5K or 4K at 60Hz via DisplayLink, plus two HDMI, two DisplayPort, Gigabit Ethernet and five USB ports. It works with M1 through M4 Macs and Windows and sits in the $100-200 bucket.

It ranks third because DisplayLink needs a driver, unlike the driverless Plugable, though it adds higher power and more outputs.

It suits Mac users across several chip generations. The caveat is the driver install.
pros: Works with M1 to M4 Macs
products.idealFor: Mac users wanting two high-res displays.

products.name: Anker Nano 13-in-1 Laptop Docking Station, 100W Max PD
products.verdict: A compact hub with a detachable 6-in-1 section.
products.description:
The Anker Nano is a 13-in-1 dock with 100W max PD, three displays through two HDMI and one DisplayPort, a 10Gbps USB-C port, three USB-A ports and a detachable 6-in-1 hub. It has a card reader, Ethernet and audio, and sits in the $100-200 bucket.

It ranks fourth because the detachable hub is clever but the 100W is a maximum, not a guarantee, and the Plugable adds certification.

It suits people who travel with part of the dock. The caveat is the three-display setup spreading bandwidth.

products.name: UGREEN 7-in-1 Docking Station Dual Monitor, Revodok Pro, 100W PD
products.verdict: Dual 4K in a small aluminum hub at a low price.
products.description:
The UGREEN Revodok Pro is a 7-in-1 dock rated for 100W PD with dual 4K at 60Hz over HDMI, 10Gbps USB-A and USB-C ports, and an aluminum compact build. It sits in the $25-50 bucket.

It ranks fifth because seven ports is thin next to the 13-in-1 docks above, but the price is a fraction.

It suits travel and light desks. The caveat is the limited port count.
products.skipIf: You need Ethernet and many ports.

products.name: Acer Laptop Docking Station, 11-in-1, 100W PD
products.verdict: Three-monitor support at a very low price.
products.description:
The Acer 11-in-1 is rated for 100W PD, supports three monitors with 8K over DisplayPort and 4K at 60Hz over HDMI, and offers 10Gbps data, 1Gbps Ethernet and an SD/TF card reader. It sits in the $25-50 bucket.

It ranks last because it carries no premium certification and the spec sheet is the thinnest on detail. The price makes it a good gamble.

It suits budget triple-monitor desks. The caveat is the lack of certification.

whatMatters.detail: A dock's wattage is often a shared pool across all ports. If the laptop gets only part of it, charging slows under load. Look for the wording laptop charging in the listing.
Thunderbolt certification guarantees bandwidth, while plain USB-C docks vary. This matters for dual high-resolution displays. Search the listing for the word certified.
DisplayLink adds extra screens through software. It needs a driver and can lag with video. Check whether the listing mentions DisplayLink.
Resolution and refresh rate caps differ with the number of monitors. Three screens often drop refresh. Read the exact combination.
Count USB-A, USB-C, Ethernet and card readers. A small dock saves space but limits devices. Match ports to your gear.

howToChoose.intro: Your laptop decides how much dock you need.

cards.label: Thunderbolt
cards.text: Verified bandwidth with no drivers. The Plugable Thunderbolt 4 dock is the example.

cards.label: USB-C
cards.text: More ports for less, with varied performance. The Anker, WAVLINK, UGREEN and Acer docks are USB-C.

howToChoose.note: Most Mac buyers should default to Thunderbolt.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: Reliable 100W laptop charging, Ethernet and a driverless setup.

cards.label: In this ranking
cards.text: The Plugable and Anker Prime both include Ethernet, and the Plugable is driverless.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You need verified bandwidth or 130W and above, pointing to the Plugable or Anker Prime.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: You only need basic dual 4K, where the UGREEN Revodok Pro works.

faq.q: Will a 100W dock charge my laptop fully?
faq.a: Only if it matches your laptop's needs. Check the charger rating.
Assuming all USB-C docks match Thunderbolt.

faq.q: Is the Plugable worth it over the UGREEN?
faq.a: If you rely on certified bandwidth and want a driverless setup.
For DisplayLink docks like the WAVLINK, yes.
The Anker Nano and Acer list three-monitor support.

faq.q: Does it need its own power?
faq.a: Yes, docks with this wattage ship with an adapter.

finalTake: The Plugable Thunderbolt 4 dock is the best 100W dock for Mac and verified performance. The Anker Prime wins for heavy charging, and the WAVLINK suits dual high-res screens. The UGREEN and Acer docks keep costs down. Check the wattage wording before you buy.
